open_items.detail: Seven definitions are printed as fact, one per line at 54, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59 and 60 (each hashed on its own: line 54 SHA-256 516018a5fb0870513529e212219b90c85b12baa8b8c97c70c67c91cfa9ff18e9; line 55 SHA-256 d28088d625bde806955b004d2c11d6da0d8e58f0caeed8f55004eeb8c0c85031; line 56 SHA-256 0b998b7a0a130bf8a892f8950ca2bc53112cebe0c9b7955380fbf9eeb074b4a3; line 57 SHA-256 23e526cc4f58ad73b6216908b57aacf9be1e3b30f85a0c16d97bbd882f7dca58; line 58 SHA-256 70584daf0ee471514a2a57b6ec0f47275edd080c477bad890ff73ae2ad186adb; line 59 SHA-256 670b52090ef840419e1eaeb599afd902b48c8bf6c6ad10e3d08b57a9cc11e850; line 60 SHA-256 dbdf60fa06054d1339489ec17fcf109b3e31523b17d1fe896f0d559f1c2a8431). Each carries an author and, for five of them, a year: Adam Smith 1776 with the claim that he is called the Father of Economics, John Stuart Mill 1843, the spelling Alfred Marshal for 1890, the spellings H. J. Daven Port and Edvins Canon with no year, A.I. Pigou with no year, and Professor Lionel C. Robins 1932 described as the most acceptable and widely used definition. None of these quotations, dates, spellings or attributions has been checked against any authority, and the popularity claim and the two reasons at lines 61-62 are the source opinion, not a verified fact.
open_items.required_action: ECON-FACT-T1-DEFINITIONS verifies every quotation, date, spelling and attribution against authoritative sources and records the effective date of each check.
